newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian diamond producer said to owe power company.
newsitem.headline: Russian diamond producer said to owe power company.

text.p: Russia's largest diamond producer Almazy Rossii-Sakha (ARS, or Diamonds of Russia-Sakha) owes 400 billion roubles ($74.1 million) to a Siberian power utility, Itar-Tass news agency quoted a striking union leader as saying on Monday.

Tass indirectly quoted Nikolai Tkachev, chairman of the Elektroprofsoyuz power workers union, in Sakha Republic, or Yakutia, as saying ARS owed 400 billion roubles in unpaid bills to the electricity company.
Moscow representatives of ARS were not available for comment.

De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd signed an agreement with Russia in February giving De Beers selling rights to one half of Russia's rough diamond output. De Beers and ARS are in negotiations for a three-year export deal.
ARS is Russia's sole authorised diamond exporter.

Workers at AO Yakutenergo, the local utility in the remote northeast Siberian region, went on strike on Monday, calling for Yakutenergo to pay workers back wages and for local industry to pay delayed power bills to Yakutenergo.
Tkachev said power workers on September 30 would cut off even emergency supplies to debtors who did not take steps to pay their bills.
Power cuts in Sakha's capital, Yakutsk, caused temporary blackouts, news reports said.
But Interfax news agency reported that diamond-producing areas in Western Yakutia had not been affected.
It said that workers at Yakutenergo were owed almost 180 billion roubles in back wages.
